name: Lake Kissimmee
type: Big, shallow grass lake: hydrilla, eelgrass, maidencane, reeds and pads
pool: Regulated by the water management district;Drawn down every few years for habitat work
notes: Pre-spawn: bass move from outside grass to inside lanes.
Peak pre-spawn. Big fish in the reeds and maidencane.
Post-spawn. Shellcracker spawn on the full moon.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: topwater early, then mats and offshore grass.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Short bites at dawn and around storms.
Shad move shallow as the nights cool.
Fall feed. Bass school on shad in creeks and canals.
Cold fronts start the speck bite offshore.
Cold fronts. Bass on outside grass; specks school in open water.

flbass.doing: Early pre-spawn: bass stage on the outside grass lines.
how: A shiner under a float beside a reed clump.

specks.doing: Specks school in open water over the deepest flats, channels and offshore grass, suspended at a different depth from day to day.
how: Missouri minnows or grass shrimp, or spider-rig small jigs (hair jigs, tubes, Hal Flies).
Set minnows at several depths, then match the one that bites.
Cast a small jig to schools you see on forward-facing sonar.

bream.doing: Slow. Bluegill and shellcracker hold in deeper grass, canals and around docks; warm, sunny afternoons bring them up.
how: Grass shrimp on the bottom next to hydrilla or eelgrass.
Small jig or worm along canal edges and docks.

flbass.doing: January: bass move from the outside grass toward the inside lanes. February is peak pre-spawn, with big fish in pencil reeds and maidencane in 2 to 4 ft.
how: Red lipless or flat-sided crankbait ticking the grass; slow down after fronts.
Beavers and jigs into pencil reeds and maidencane.
Wild shiners on the outside edge for big fish.

specks.doing: Schools leave the open water for pad fields, bulrush and Kissimmee grass that sit next to deeper water. A cold front pushes them back out.
how: Troll or drift minnow-tipped jigs along the outside of the pads and reeds.
Minnow under a cork in openings at the grass edge.
Fish the closest open water off the same grass.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

flbass.doing: March is the heavy spawn. Sight-fish in clear water; in stained water, work the dark spots in the pad fields.
how: Compact plastics pitched to dark spots.
Weightless stick bait, paused and twitched.

specks.doing: Specks spawn in pads, bulrush, cattails and Kissimmee grass over sandy bottom, in waves around the full moon, usually at about 60 to 65°F.
how: Minnow or grass shrimp under a small cork in pockets and along reed lines.
A 10 to 14 ft pole and a 1/32 to 1/16 oz jig dipped into holes in the pads.
Fish the closest deeper water off the spawning grass.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

flbass.doing: April is post-spawn feeding along reeds, riprap and eelgrass. In May, bluegill beds near reeds and pads set off midday topwater bites, and bass roam offshore hydrilla.
how: Buzzbait, walking bait or swim jig along reeds and eelgrass.
Wacky rig or fluke around shade.
Popper or prop bait over the colonies.

specks.doing: After the spawn, specks scatter to deeper grass edges, docks, bridges and channel edges. The bite slows as the water warms.
how: Minnows at dock pilings, bridges and fish attractors.
Small jig swum along the deep edge of the vegetation.

bream.doing: Bluegill bed in colonies on sand around each full moon from April on: the best bream fishing of the year, with fish near a pound on good lakes.
how: Under a cork over the beds or along reed lines.
In deep spatterdock and grass patches.
Popping bug or small spider at dawn and dusk.

flbass.doing: Frogs early and late over the cheese mats, then punch hyacinth when the sun is high. Wind and storms set off short feeding windows.
how: Frog early and late; punch with 1 to 1.25 oz when the sun is high.
Speed worm or vibrating jig along eelgrass.
Big worm along the outside grass.
Keep a spinnerbait ready for outflows after a storm.

specks.doing: The slowest season. Specks suspend in the deepest water, on fish attractors and in shade; fish early, late or at night.
how: Lights and minnows at bridges and deep docks.
Vertical jig or minnow at the depth you mark.

bream.doing: Bluegill keep spawning on each full moon; between moons they hold in deeper pads, grass patches and around docks. Fish early.
how: Grass shrimp in deep pads and hydrilla patches; anchor and chum lightly.
Worms and crickets along the walkways.

flbass.doing: Young shad move shallow in September. By October, wind-blown eelgrass and hydrilla edges fish all day; in November bass return to the outside edges.
how: Small walking bait, squarebill or finesse swimbait in the backs of flats.
Vibrating jig and lipless crankbait, then a Texas rig where fish are nipping.
Jerkbait or lipless crankbait on sparse hydrilla on bright days; jig on isolated reeds in wind.

specks.doing: The first good cold fronts start the speck bite. Schools gather in open water and around fish attractors, then slide toward the pads as it cools.
how: Jigs and minnows across open water near drop-offs.
Vertical jig, keeping baits above the brush.
Bright jigs in clear water, dark in tannic or stained water.

bream.doing: Bluegill pick up as the water cools, around Bird, Brahma, Rabbit and Grassy islands.
how: Live bait in open water near the vegetation.
Fish the edges of bulrush, cattail and pondweed beds.

zones.name: North-end flats and river mouth
zones.t: Where the chain flows in: outside grass at daybreak, then isolated reeds in 2 to 4 ft.

zones.name: West-shore grass walls
zones.t: Long maidencane walls and eelgrass lanes; fish corners and points.

zones.name: South end toward SR 60
zones.t: FWC names the stretch from the fish camps to the Rocks.

zones.name: Offshore hydrilla and eelgrass
zones.t: Idle to find the thick clumps, then fan-cast.

zones.name: Mats in the coves
zones.t: Hyacinth and pennywort against hard edges or wood.

zones.name: Open water, mid-lake
zones.t: Drift or troll near offshore grass.

zones.name: Mixed grass
zones.t: Where several kinds of plants grow together.

zones.name: The islands
zones.t: Bird, Brahma and Rabbit islands as the water cools.

zones.name: Reed and sand flats
zones.t: Shellcracker, then bluegill bed colonies near reeds and sand.

zones.name: Deep grass edges
zones.t: Suspended specks off the offshore grass.
